title: Refactor admission controller and hotkey propagation; remove scheduler spinlocks; dependency refresh
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Our continuous-batching admission path and hotkey propagation (notifications used to prime KV cache shards) have accumulated several small hacks that increase tail latency and complicate scheduler reasoning. Additionally, the scheduler currently uses a light-weight spinlock around its slot allocator which shows contention on 64+ core GPU hosts during throughput spikes. This ticket is a focused refactor to: 1) Extract a dedicated admission-controller module with clear backpressure/admission policies; 2) Replace hotkey propagation hooks with a publish/subscribe priming conduit that de-duplicates priming requests and records priming TTLs; 3) Remove the scheduler spinlock and replace with a hybrid MCS/lockfree freelist; 4) Upgrade two build-time dependencies (protobuf -> 3.23.4, jemalloc -> 5.3.0) that unblock safer memory accounting APIs used by the new allocator.
acceptance_criteria: New admission-controller module accepts requests and enforces per-route concurrency limits identical to baseline under steady state
Hotkey priming reduces duplicate KV cache priming RPCs by >= 40% for our benchmark hotkey distribution
Scheduler no longer uses the global spinlock; contention metric (spinwait_ns) drops by >75% under 64-core stress scenario
End-to-end P99 latency for 512-token gen under packed workload is not worse than baseline +5%
All unit and integration tests pass; migration flag gates new code-paths
Upgrade PRs merged and CI green; packaging smoke tests pass for Dedicated and Private builds
implementation_notes: Plan: 1) Implement admission controller API (admit/reject/queue) with pluggable policy; 2) Implement priming conduit that deduplicates by (model, shard, hotkey-hash) and attaches a short-lived lease; 3) Replace slot allocator spinlock: introduce MCS lock for cross-node fairness and a per-core freelist for fast path; 4) Wire memory-accounting to jemalloc introspection APIs removed in old build; 5) Upgrade protobuf to 3.23.4 and adapt generated bindings in the priming RPCs. Rollout: feature-flagged and staged: unit tests -> internal canary (dev cluster) -> dedicated canary (us-west2) -> 10% prod -> full. Backout: feature flag off, runtime falls back to legacy admission path and old priming conduit.
risks_and_mitigation: Dependency upgrade may break binary compatibility: keep protobuf update in separate PR and run a flattened compatibility test suite
Priming dedupe could increase cold-cache duration if TTLs mis-tuned: start with conservative TTL (30s) and monitor miss rates
Scheduler change could regress throughput on small instances: add microbench harnesses and a canary with identical traffic to verify
Rollout complexity: use feature flags + health checks + automated rollback on error-rate spike
tasks: ENG-53321-1: Add admission-controller interface and tests
ENG-53321-2: Implement priming conduit and TTL store

ENG-53321-4: Upgrade protobuf and jemalloc; update CI images

notes: This refactor aims to reduce tail latency and simplify future work on automatic rerouting and capacity-aware admission. Keep changes small and feature-flagged to make rollbacks straightforward. Coordinate with SDK and Console teams for any metric name changes.
